articles.title: Hearts 'have to be above emotions' as big favourites in cup
articles.summary: Hearts head coach Wouter Vrancken insists there can be no excuses as his side prepare to face Stenhousemuir at Ochilview on Friday with a place in the Premier Sports Cup semi-finals at stake.
body: The Tynecastle side are unbeaten in their past eight matches, but Vrancken is wary of the challenge posed by the surprise Scottish Championship leaders on their own artificial surface at Ochilview.

"It's not about Astro, it's not about stadium, it's not about all those things. Excuses are for losers, let's say," Vrancken said as he demands the same focus shown in the recent Edinburgh derby and European qualifiers.
"You have to prepare, you have to prepare yourself and you have to be ready. You have to cope with those things and be ready and be above.
"Like I told the players also before the Hibs game, we have to be above the emotions.

articles.title: Why David Beckham will have my vote for the US Soccer Hall of Fame | Pablo Iglesias Maurer
articles.summary: The Englishman has gotten no shortage of recognition, but his contributions to the American game deserve an official title. Sign up for our free newsletter here. Next spring, when the US Soccer Hall of Fame welcomes its newest class, there will be pomp and circumstance.
body: Many involved will be American-born soccer legends, of course. Yet every once in a while, a player whose footprint extends well beyond the borders of the United States graces the stage. Such may be the case next year when the hall potentially welcomes English legend David Beckham into the fold.

Some readers abroad – and certainly plenty of readers here in the States – will wonder why an ostensibly American Hall of Fame would admit non-Americans, something it’s done since its inception. The answer lies in the nature of the American game itself. Even our earliest heroes – Joe Gaetjens and the like – were immigrants, with Gaetjens scoring his famed goal against England in the 1950 World Cup when he wasn’t even a US citizen (he never ended up becoming one).

articles.title: Two forehands, no backhands: meet the US Open’s fascinating ambidextrous experiment
articles.summary: Teo Davidov doesn’t hit backhands. He serves from both sides. The 16-year-old from Denver is treating the tennis world to a wildly unorthodox style – and proving it’s more than a parlor trick. Teo Davidov always has the upper hands.
body: Teo Davidov always has the upper hands. An amiable junior prodigy from Denver, the 16-year-old was the oddest sight at this year’s US Open, the only player in the tournament – man, woman or junior – who hits only forehands. To be clear: it’s not that he doesn’t have a backhand or can’t hit a backhand. He’s ambidextrous and so he doesn’t bother with them.

It’s nothing personal. “To be honest, I like the traditional backhand-forehand,” he says. “I like the classiness of it. I like hitting backhands myself just to play around, just for fun.” He hits those from both wings, too.

Davidov has been a giddy curiosity for hardcore tennis fans for the past five years, with rubberneckers gaping at clips from his matches and training sessions that seem at a glance like AI. A four-year-old video of him flummoxing Carlos Alcaraz’s younger brother makes for especially tasty viewing. “I don’t really look at the comments or things like that,” Davidoff says. “But I’ve heard most people online just always have something they think might not work.”

articles.title: Team GB return after pregnancy 'hard to put into words' - Kinsella
articles.summary: A year after giving birth, Alice Kinsella takes the latest step on her groundbreaking return to gymnastics at an international meeting for Team GB.
body: Olympic gymnast Alice Kinsella says "it's hard to put into words" how she feels about returning to international competition as her groundbreaking comeback to the sport continues this weekend.
The two-time European champion became the first British artistic gymnast to resume elite competition after giving birth, when she finished fourth in the beam at the British Championships in March.

Now the 25-year-old is preparing for her first competition back in Team GB colours at a senior team international against France, Switzerland, Germany and Italy at Fenton Manor in Stoke on 12-13 September.
"It's kind of crazy - it's such a surreal feeling but I am very excited," Kinsella told BBC Radio Stoke.

articles.title: 'The fastest kid alive': 5 things to know about UTSA football, Texas State's I-35 rival
articles.summary: Texas State football can't afford to dwell on the 59-7 drubbing the Texas Longhorns handed it. Not when UTSA visits for the home opener. The Bobcats have won the I-35 Rivalry two years in a row. They stomped the Roadrunners 49-10 in 2024 and notched a 43-36 win inside the Alamodome last season.
body: The teams' familiarity goes far back. UTSA head coach Jeff Traylor and Texas State head coach GJ Kinne share a close bond that dates to Kinne's days playing quarterback for Traylor in high school. The two schools compete in recruiting across the state, and the back-and-forth between the fans has already begun on social media.
Back in Kinne's day at Tulsa, abut 15 years ago, a quarterback staying with one program for three seasons was relatively common. It's far from the norm nowadays.

UTSA quarterback Owen McCown is one of those rare three-year starters. He's thrown for 6,419 yards and 55 touchdowns as a Roadrunner. Rick Bowie is UTSA's new offensive coordinator and is said to incorporate a more vertical passing attack.
"You can kind of see how (McCown's) progressed each year," Kinne said.

articles.title: Beloved hockey legend Barry Melrose, who played and coached the Adirondack Red Wings, dies at 70
articles.summary: Former NHL coach and popular ESPN analyst Barry Melrose, who played for and coached the American Hockey League's Adirondack Red Wings in Glens Falls, died Wednesday at 70 years old. Melrose retired from ESPN after he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in 2023.
body: Melrose, a native of Kelvington, Saskatchewan, was an Adirondack defenseman from 1983-87 and coached the Red Wings from 1989-92. He also played in 300 NHL games with Winnipeg, Toronto and Detroit.
He helped the Red Wings win the Calder Cup as a player in 1985-86 and as head coach in 1991-92.

The following season, Melrose was hired as head coach of the Los Angeles Kings. He guided the Kings to the 1993 Stanley Cup Finals, where they lost to the Montreal Canadiens. He spent three years with the Kings.
Hired by ESPN in 1996, Melrose was beloved by hockey fans, both for his personality and his mullet hairstyle.

articles.title: Leclerc takes blame for Hamilton clash at Monza after Ferrari talks
articles.summary: Charles Leclerc has admitted "I didn't behave the way I should have" when racing Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton at the opening lap of the Italian Grand Prix.
body: Hamilton accused the team of having "no rules" after he was forced wide by Leclerc at the exit of the first chicane, an incident which cost him six positions, and could only recover to sixth place at Ferrari's home event.
Ahead of this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid, both drivers discussed the incident with Ferrari chairman John Elkann, chief executive Benedetto Vigna and team principal Frederic Vasseur.

"What was very important was to speak first of all. It's been quite a few years now that I've been in Ferrari and I know how it feels when everything on Ferrari is kind of on fire and if you don't speak between Lewis and I, you can get caught with this noise around the team," said Leclerc.

"It's not that there's no reason for that noise but the intensity of the noise is a bit too crazy. When you look at Monza, there has been friction between other team-mates and we barely talk about it but when it's about Ferrari, it takes proportion that is not normal.

articles.title: Drury Panthers volleyball players Bray, Hilton snag GLVC weekly awards
articles.summary: After guiding Drury volleyball to a 4-0 weekend at the SBU Invitational, Panthers junior Jacy Bray and sophomore Skylar Hilton have been named the Athletic Solutions Great Lakes Valley Conference Setter and Offensive Player of the Week, the league office announced Tuesday, Sept. 8.
body: Bray, who totaled 129 assists (10.75 per set) in fueling Drury's sweep of its four matches in Bolivar, becomes the first Panther ever to earn a GLVC Setter of the Week honor. The junior from Nixa stretched her streak of consecutive double-digit assist totals to 31 in a row (dating back to Sept. 12, 2025), pacing a Panther offense record the No. 2 hitting percentage (.254) and kill average (13.96 per set) in the GLVC.

Bray registered 33 assists and a season-best two service aces against Arkansas-Monticello, then posted 39 helpers, eight digs and a career-high three kills vs. East Central to help DU to its sixth consecutive straight-set victory.

Hilton delivered team-leading totals of 29 kills and 11 blocks to go along with a blistering.538 hitting percentage over Drury's four wins at SBU, extending its best start to a season in nine years (7-1). The sophomore from Ozark matched a season high with 11 kills in Drury's victory over Christian Brothers on Saturday, Sept. 5, after hitting a season best.692 in DU's tournament opener vs. Arkansas-Monticello the previous afternoon.

articles.title: Premier League fixtures: Bumper festive period announced
articles.summary: The Premier League's festive fixtures have been announced for this season - with 29 matches available to watch live on Sky Sports between Boxing Day and January 7.
body: England's top-flight have announced the festive fixtures more than three months in advance as it "gives supporters notice to plan and make travel arrangements for a particularly busy time of the year".
It also follows consultation with the Football Supporters' Association and representatives from club Fan Advisory Boards.

There will be seven Premier League matches on Boxing Day this year, with Hull City vs Liverpool - kicking off at 5.30pm - and Newcastle vs Man City - kicking off at 8pm - featuring as a live Sky Sports double header.

A triple header on Sky Sports then follows on Super Sunday on December 27, with Frank Lampard taking on Chelsea as Coventry boss at 2pm. That match is then followed by Manchester United vs Nottingham Forest at 4.30pm, then Crystal Palace vs Arsenal at 7pm.

articles.title: Waardah impresses with Park Hill win
articles.summary: First-time headgear worked the oracle for Owen Burrows’ Waardah who ran out an ultimately impressive winner of the Betfred Park Hill Stakes at Doncaster.
body: The Owen Burrows-trained Waardah took top honours in the feature Park Hill Fillies' Stakes on the opening day of Doncaster's St Leger Festival, with Callum Rodriguez in the saddle.
Sporting a hood for the first time in a race, she was more tractable for Callum Rodriguez and she added another Group Two win to her record having landed the Lillie Langtry at Goodwood last season.
The heatwave has hampered her progress this summer as she prefers some cut in the ground and when third in the same Goodwood event last month, that was just her second start of the season.
Burrows is now eyeing a possible bid for a Group One double, with the Prix de Royallieu on Arc weekend at ParisLongchamp and Champions Day at Ascot both on his radar.
